newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: First Prov, Northern, Sunstate to merge.
newsitem.headline: First Prov, Northern, Sunstate to merge.

text.p: Queensland building societies First Provincial Building Society Ltd and Northern Building Society said on Thursday they planned a three-way amalgamation with Sunstate Credit Union to create First Australian Building Society.
They said the combined group would be the largest building society in Queensland with estimated total assets of over A$1.1 billion, 470 staff and 220,000 members.
Under the terms of the deal, Northern and First Provincial shareholders would hold one share in First Australian Building Society for each share presently held.
First Provincial, which is expected to be the one continuing entity, said it would separately offer Sunstate qualifying members four million First Provincial shares at A$1.20 per share.
The shares issued to Sunstate would rank equally with all other shares for dividends, including an eight cent dividend expected to be paid in October 1997.
"In addition a one-off special dividend of 70 cents per share is to be paid on these shares on or before 31 December 1999," First Provincial said.
The proposal is subject to the required approvals under the Financial Institutions Code, the Prudential Standards being obtained and the finalisation of the due diligence review by August 22

"The directors of First Provincial and Sunstate believe that the amalgamation of the two organisations will provide significant economies of scale and a wider range of products and more competitive benefits for members," First Provincial said.

First Provincial and Northern, who flagged a merger in late June, said they expected cost savings relating to the three-way amalgamation of about A$5 million for the full year or A$2.8 million for the year to June 30, 1998.

"Based on 1997/98 budgets, full year earnings incorporating all rationalisation benefits are estimated to be approximately 27 cents per share, but as the merger will only take effect during Octoberr 1997, 1997/98 earnings are estimated at about 23 cents.
Meetings of members of the First Provincial and Northern to approve the amalgamation are expected to be held by the end of October.
First Pacific's shares were untraded on Thursday morning, having closed up one cent at A$2.50 on Wednesday.
